affected_objects.before: This association product represents the operational assignment of volunteers to fundraising events. It captures the specific role, shift timing, and attendance tracking for each volunteer serving at each event. Each record links one fundraising event to one volunteer with attributes that exist only in the context of this assignment relationship, enabling event staffing management, volunteer coordination, and post-event reporting.. Existence Justification: Fundraising events require multiple volunteers serving in different operational roles (registration, setup, catering, cleanup), and volunteers serve at multiple events throughout the year. The nonprofit actively manages event volunteer assignments as a distinct operational process, coordinating staffing needs, assigning specific roles and shifts, tracking attendance via check-in/check-out, and recording hours worked for each volunteer at each event. This is not a derived correlation but an operational entity that event managers create, update, and monitor.

Covers all assessment types including FGD (Focus Group Discussion), KII (Key Informant Interview), household survey, rapid needs assessment, PDM (Post-Distribution Monitoring) with linked distribution event and utilization/adequacy scoring, market assessment, and MUAC screening. Captures assessment date, project site, methodology, target population, sample size, assessment team, KoboToolbox or CommCare form ID, data collection tool, key findings summary, recommendations, and assessment status (planned, in-progress, completed, validated). Links to assessment_response for individual submissions. Supports MEL indicator tracking, SitRep generation, CHS compliance, accountability to affected populations (AAP), and donor reporting on program quality.

became.before: This association product represents the participation relationship between field assessments and volunteers who serve as enumerators or team members. It captures the operational reality that assessments are conducted by multi-person teams, and volunteers participate in multiple assessments over time. Each record links one assessment to one volunteer with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific participation: the volunteer's role in that assessment, their performance metrics, and training completion status for that particular assessment methodology.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit field operations, assessments (FGDs, KIIs, household surveys, PDM, MUAC screening) are conducted by multi-person enumerator teams, and volunteers participate in multiple assessments over time across different projects and methodologies. The business actively manages assessment participation as an operational entity: field coordinators recruit volunteers for specific assessments, assign roles (lead vs. enumerator), track data quality scores per volunteer per assessment, verify methodology-specific training completion, and use this data for volunteer performance management and future assignment decisions.
became.after: Assessment Participation - core entity in the field domain supporting humanitarian operations.

affected_objects.before: This association product represents the participation relationship between field assessments and volunteers who serve as enumerators or team members. It captures the operational reality that assessments are conducted by multi-person teams, and volunteers participate in multiple assessments over time. Each record links one assessment to one volunteer with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific participation: the volunteer's role in that assessment, their performance metrics, and training completion status for that particular assessment methodology.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit field operations, assessments (FGDs, KIIs, household surveys, PDM, MUAC screening) are conducted by multi-person enumerator teams, and volunteers participate in multiple assessments over time across different projects and methodologies. The business actively manages assessment participation as an operational entity: field coordinators recruit volunteers for specific assessments, assign roles (lead vs. enumerator), track data quality scores per volunteer per assessment, verify methodology-specific training completion, and use this data for volunteer performance management and future assignment decisions.
affected_objects.after: Assessment Participation - core entity in the field domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Logical Framework (LogFrame) master records defining the results chain hierarchy for each program or grant. Each logframe captures the full intervention logic: goal (impact), purpose (outcome), outputs, activities, assumptions, risks, and objectively verifiable indicators (OVIs) at each level. Includes Theory of Change (ToC) components as embedded rows within the hierarchy. Aligns with DAC evaluation criteria, RBM standards, and donor-specific logframe templates (DFID/FCDO, USAID, EU, ECHO). Links to indicator targets for performance tracking and supports results framework reporting.

became.before: This association product represents the Bid or Quotation submitted by a vendor in response to a Request for Quotation (RFQ). It captures the complete bid submission including pricing, technical proposal, evaluation scores, and award decision. Each record links one RFQ to one vendor with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific bid submission. Essential for procurement audit trails, competitive bidding transparency, and donor compliance reporting per 2 CFR 200 procurement standards.. Existence Justification: In humanitarian procurement operations, RFQs are issued to multiple vendors during competitive bidding processes, and each vendor submits a formal bid with pricing, technical proposals, and delivery terms. affected_objects.before: This association product represents the Bid or Quotation submitted by a vendor in response to a Request for Quotation (RFQ). It captures the complete bid submission including pricing, technical proposal, evaluation scores, and award decision. Each record links one RFQ to one vendor with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific bid submission. Essential for procurement audit trails, competitive bidding transparency, and donor compliance reporting per 2 CFR 200 procurement standards.. Existence Justification: In humanitarian procurement operations, RFQs are issued to multiple vendors during competitive bidding processes, and each vendor submits a formal bid with pricing, technical proposals, and delivery terms. The business actively manages each bid submission through evaluation scoring, ranking, and award decisions. This is not a simple reference but an operational business entity that procurement officers create, evaluate, and audit for donor compliance per 2 CFR 200 standards.
affected_objects.after: Bid - core entity in the supply domain supporting humanitarian operations.

affected_objects.before: Master catalog of all humanitarian commodities and relief items managed in the supply chain, including NFIs (Non-Food Items), medical supplies, WASH materials, food commodities, shelter materials, and emergency relief goods. Defines item specifications, unit of measure, commodity category (e.g., shelter, health, nutrition, WASH), SPHERE standards compliance, shelf life, storage requirements (temperature, humidity), hazardous classification, kit/assembly composition (bill of materials for NFI kits), cold-chain requirements, donor restrictions, and procurement lead time. This is the SSOT for all commodity definitions used across procurement, warehousing, and distribution.
affected_objects.after: Commodity - core entity in the supply domain supporting humanitarian operations.
structure_pinned=true,domain=supply,domain_verified=true

affected_objects.before: This association product represents the prequalification and supply agreement between a humanitarian commodity and a partner organization. It captures the partner's capacity and terms to supply specific commodities, including agreed pricing, lead times, quality certifications, and historical performance. Each record links one commodity to one partner organization with attributes that exist only in the context of this supply relationship. Used for sourcing decisions, RFQ targeting, and localization strategy in humanitarian procurement.. Existence Justification: In humanitarian supply chain operations, partner organizations are prequalified to supply specific commodities based on capacity assessments, certifications, and past performance. A single commodity (e.g., water purification tablets) can be sourced from multiple prequalified partners at different unit costs and lead times, and a single partner organization can supply multiple different commodities (e.g., WASH items, shelter materials, medical supplies). The business actively manages these supply agreements as operational records with partner-specific pricing, lead times, quality certifications, and performance ratings.
affected_objects.after: Commodity Supply Agreement - core entity in the supply domain supporting humanitarian operations.

affected_objects.before: Operational order authorizing the release and dispatch of commodities from a warehouse to a field distribution point for beneficiary delivery. Captures order number, originating distribution plan, issuing warehouse, destination distribution point, commodity lines with quantities, dispatch date, transport mode, waybill reference, loading officer, and order status (draft/approved/dispatched/delivered/closed). Triggers stock movement and last-mile logistics execution.

Captures distribution plan name, target program, geographic coverage (country/admin levels), planned distribution date range, target beneficiary count, commodity list with planned quantities per beneficiary, distribution modality (direct/voucher/cash-in-kind), responsible field office, and approval status. Links supply chain planning to field operations and MEL targets.

affected_objects.before: This association product represents the line-item relationship between distribution plans and commodities in humanitarian supply chain operations. It captures the bill of materials for each distribution event, specifying which commodities are included in each distribution plan with planned quantities, priorities, and allocation details. Each record links one distribution plan to one commodity with attributes that exist only in the context of this specific plan-commodity pairing.. Existence Justification: In humanitarian supply chain operations, distribution plans specify a bill of materials (list of commodities with quantities) for each distribution event. A single distribution plan includes multiple commodities (e.g., shelter kits, water purification tablets, blankets, food rations), and each commodity appears in multiple distribution plans across different programs, locations, and time periods. The business actively manages these plan-commodity pairings with specific quantities, priorities, allocation statuses, and cost estimates.

Critical for humanitarian rapid-response procurement where pre-negotiated LTAs enable emergency purchase orders within 24-72 hours without full competitive bidding. Supports 2 CFR 200 sole-source justification documentation.

Procurement officers actively manage line-item details including per-line quantities, vendor pricing, delivery schedules, and receipt tracking—this is the operational record that drives three-way matching and inventory management.

became.before: Captures the end-to-end recruitment and onboarding application lifecycle for prospective volunteers. Tracks application submission date, recruitment channel, program of interest, screening status, background check outcome, reference check status, interview notes, acceptance or rejection decision, and onboarding completion milestones. Supports the Volunteer and Staff Recruitment and Management core business process.
became.after: Application - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Unified competency and credential product — the single source of truth for all skills taxonomy and individual volunteer credentials within the volunteer domain. As REFERENCE CATALOG: defines skill categories (medical, logistics, language, psychosocial, WASH, ICT4D, community mobilization), proficiency levels, role-to-skill requirements, and mandatory vs. preferred designations for volunteer_role entries. As INDIVIDUAL RECORDS: tracks specific credentials held by each volunteer including professional licenses, first aid certificates, SPHERE practitioner credentials, PSEA compliance certificates, verified and self-assessed proficiency levels, issuing body, issue and expiry dates, certificate numbers, verification status, renewal requirements, and evidence document references. Supports skill-based volunteer matching, competency gap analysis, compliance tracking, deployment readiness assessment, and training needs identification.
became.after: Certification - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Records data protection consents, safeguarding declarations, and policy acknowledgments provided by volunteers. Captures consent type (data processing consent, image/likeness release, safeguarding code of conduct acknowledgment, background check authorization, medical information sharing consent), consent date, consent version, volunteer (FK), granting method (digital signature, wet signature, verbal recorded), consent status (active, withdrawn, expired), withdrawal date and reason, legal basis under applicable data protection regulation (GDPR, local DPA), retention period, and associated deployment or program context. Supports GDPR Article 7 compliance, organizational safeguarding policies, and donor due diligence requirements for volunteer data handling in humanitarian operations.
became.after: Consent - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.
volunteer_registry
structure_contract=required,structure_pinned=true,domain=volunteer,domain_verified=true

became.before: Captures structured feedback submitted by volunteers about their deployment experience, training quality, organizational support, supervision, and overall satisfaction. Distinct from beneficiary feedback (owned by communication domain) — this product is exclusively for volunteer voice. Records feedback submission date, feedback channel (survey, FGD, KII, digital form), program or deployment context (FK to volunteer_deployment), satisfaction ratings across dimensions (support, communication, impact, safety), qualitative comments, anonymization flag, and follow-up action status. Supports MEAL accountability mechanisms, volunteer retention improvement, and CHS commitment to people management.
became.after: Feedback - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Authoritative transactional record of volunteer hours contributed per activity, deployment, or event — the timesheet equivalent for unpaid contributors. Captures log date, volunteer (FK to volunteer), deployment or program context (FK to volunteer_deployment), activity type, location, hours claimed, hours verified, verification method (supervisor sign-off, digital check-in/GPS, self-reported), approval status, approving supervisor, and notes. Primary source for donor reporting on volunteer in-kind contributions (valued at fair market rates per IRS guidelines or local equivalents), MEL indicator tracking (e.g., volunteer-hours per beneficiary), recognition milestone triggers, and BvA reporting on volunteer effort allocation across grants. Supports audit trail requirements for institutional donor compliance.
became.after: Hour Log - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Records safety, security, and welfare incidents involving volunteers during deployments or activities. Captures incident date, location, incident type (security threat, accident, health emergency, harassment, PSEA violation, natural hazard), severity level, volunteer(s) involved, immediate response actions taken, referral to support services, investigation status, and resolution outcome. Supports duty-of-care obligations and CHS accountability requirements. Distinct from field operations incident tracking — this is volunteer-welfare focused.
became.after: Incident Report - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Records formal and informal recognition events awarded to volunteers for contributions, milestones, and achievements. Captures recognition type (length-of-service award, outstanding contribution, skills milestone, program completion certificate, public acknowledgment, peer nomination), award date, awarding program or country office, recognition channel (ceremony, newsletter, social media, certificate), associated volunteer hours milestone threshold, nominator, and approval status. Supports volunteer retention and motivation strategies aligned with organizational volunteer engagement policy.
became.after: Recognition - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Defines the catalog of volunteer roles available across programs and field operations. Each role specifies the role title, functional area (e.g., WASH, GBV, PSS, nutrition, logistics), required skills, minimum certification requirements, physical demands, deployment context (field/office/remote), maximum concurrent assignments, and whether the role is active. Acts as the reference catalog for role-based volunteer deployment.
became.after: Role - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Manages the scheduling of volunteers for specific shifts, activities, or field assignments within a program or event. Captures schedule period, shift start and end times, location, required volunteer count, assigned volunteers (FK to volunteer), schedule status (draft, published, confirmed, cancelled), scheduling conflicts or overrides, and recurrence patterns. Enables field coordinators to plan volunteer coverage across concurrent programs, manage shift swaps, and communicate rosters. Integrates with volunteer availability attributes on the volunteer master for conflict detection.
became.after: Schedule - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Manages non-salary financial support provided to volunteers including transport allowances, meal allowances, communication stipends, per diem, and in-kind support (NFIs, protective equipment). Captures stipend type, amount or in-kind value, currency, payment period and frequency, payment method (mobile money, bank transfer, cash), approval status, disbursement date, volunteer (FK), deployment context (FK to volunteer_deployment), and grant or fund source. Distinct from payroll (workforce domain) — stipends are non-employment compensation for volunteers. Supports BvA tracking, donor reporting on volunteer support costs, and tax reporting where applicable.
became.after: Stipend - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: This association product represents the Authorization between data_collection_tool and volunteer. It captures the training, certification, and authorization lifecycle for volunteers to administer specific MEL data collection instruments. Each record links one data_collection_tool to one volunteer with attributes that track training completion, certification status, authorization validity periods, and proficiency levels - essential for quality control, compliance, and volunteer deployment planning.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit field operations, volunteers are trained and authorized to administer multiple data collection tools (ODK surveys, MUAC screening forms, KII guides, DHIS2 forms), and each tool is administered by multiple trained volunteers across different geographic locations and programs. The organization actively manages volunteer tool authorizations as a compliance and quality control process, tracking training completion, certification status, authorization validity periods, and proficiency levels for each volunteer-tool combination. This is an operational business process where MEL staff create authorization records after training, monitor expiry dates, and revoke authorizations when quality issues arise.
became.after: Tool Authorization - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Catalog of training programs, workshops, and capacity-building courses available to volunteers. Captures training title, delivery modality (in-person, e-learning, blended), training category (safety and security, technical skills, CHS orientation, SPHERE standards, GBV awareness, PSEA, first aid), duration, facilitator, accrediting body, certification awarded upon completion, and whether training is mandatory for specific roles. Distinct from the workforce LMS — this catalog is specific to volunteer capacity building.
became.after: Training - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

It captures the operational assignment of volunteers to partner organizations for specific roles, time periods, and performance tracking. Each record links one volunteer to one partner organization with attributes that exist only in the context of this deployment relationship, including role, dates, hours contributed, and performance assessment.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit operations, volunteers are deployed to multiple partner organizations over time for different projects, field placements, and programs, and each partner organization works with multiple volunteers simultaneously. It captures the organizational requirement that volunteers formally acknowledge and confirm understanding of PSEA policies, child safeguarding policies, and codes of conduct. Each record links one volunteer to one psea_policy version with attributes tracking when, how, and under what terms the acknowledgment was made, including digital signatures, expiry dates, and renewal requirements. This is a core compliance and safeguarding data product.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit safeguarding operations, volunteers must formally acknowledge multiple PSEA policies throughout their tenure: organizational policies, country-specific policies when deployed, and updated versions when policies are revised. Each policy is acknowledged by many volunteers across the organization. The acknowledgment itself is a managed compliance event with specific data (date, method, version, signature, expiry) that belongs to neither the volunteer nor the policy alone.

It captures the enrollment, completion, and certification lifecycle for each volunteer's participation in a safeguarding training program. Each record links one volunteer to one training_program with attributes that track compliance status, certification validity, and completion evidence.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit operations, volunteers complete multiple safeguarding training programs over their tenure (PSEA awareness, child protection, code of conduct, investigation procedures), and each training program is completed by hundreds or thousands of volunteers across the organization. This is a recognized operational entity called 'training completion' or 'training record' that safeguarding officers query, update, and monitor for compliance reporting.

affected_objects.before: This association product represents the Authorization between data_collection_tool and volunteer. It captures the training, certification, and authorization lifecycle for volunteers to administer specific MEL data collection instruments. Each record links one data_collection_tool to one volunteer with attributes that track training completion, certification status, authorization validity periods, and proficiency levels - essential for quality control, compliance, and volunteer deployment planning.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit field operations, volunteers are trained and authorized to administer multiple data collection tools (ODK surveys, MUAC screening forms, KII guides, DHIS2 forms), and each tool is administered by multiple trained volunteers across different geographic locations and programs. The organization actively manages volunteer tool authorizations as a compliance and quality control process, tracking training completion, certification status, authorization validity periods, and proficiency levels for each volunteer-tool combination. This is an operational business process where MEL staff create authorization records after training, monitor expiry dates, and revoke authorizations when quality issues arise.
affected_objects.after: Tool Authorization - core entity in the volunteer domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Transactional record capturing formal modifications to existing partnership agreements including scope changes, budget realignments, no-cost extensions, period of performance adjustments, and signatory changes. Tracks amendment number, amendment type, effective date, justification, approval authority, and the specific clauses modified. Maintains the full amendment history of each agreement.

became.before: This association product represents the participation relationship between partner organizations and advocacy campaigns. It captures each partner's role, contribution type, visibility level, and approval status for their involvement in specific campaigns. Each record links one partner organization to one advocacy campaign with attributes that exist only in the context of this participation relationship. This is the operational record of partner engagement in advocacy, awareness, and fundraising campaigns managed by the communications team.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit operations, partner organizations participate in multiple advocacy campaigns simultaneously (e.g., a CSO may be involved in a humanitarian access campaign, a localization advocacy initiative, and a policy reform campaign at the same time). Each advocacy campaign involves multiple partner organizations with distinct roles (lead, supporting, implementing). The communications team actively manages these participation relationships, tracking each partner's role, contribution type, visibility level, and approval status per campaign for coordination, attribution, and reporting purposes.
became.after: Campaign Participation - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.
consortium_engagement
structure_contract=required,structure_pinned=true,domain=partnership,domain_verified=true

became.before: Records formal partner capacity assessments conducted prior to or during partnership engagement. Captures assessment methodology (e.g., USAID OCA, DFID OCAT), assessment date, assessor identity, scores across functional areas (financial management, HR, procurement, governance, MEL), overall risk rating, and recommended capacity-building interventions. Essential for due diligence and risk management.
became.after: Capacity Assessment - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.
capacity_development
structure_contract=required,structure_pinned=true,domain=partnership,domain_verified=true

became.before: Transactional record for individual capacity-building activities delivered to partner organizations including trainings, mentoring sessions, technical assistance visits, and peer learning events. Captures activity type, delivery date, facilitator, participants, topics covered, pre/post assessment scores, and completion status. Tracks progress against the capacity-building plan.
became.after: Capacity Building Activity - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.
capacity_development
structure_contract=required,structure_pinned=true,domain=partnership,domain_verified=true

became.before: Master record with embedded activity line-items for structured capacity-building interventions developed for partner organizations based on capacity assessment findings. Plan-level data captures objectives, targeted functional areas (financial management, HR, procurement, governance, MEL), timeline, responsible staff, budget allocation, and overall progress status. Activity-level line-items capture individual trainings, mentoring sessions, technical assistance visits, and peer learning events with delivery dates, facilitators, participant lists, topics covered, pre/post assessment scores, and completion status. Supports localization strategies, partner strengthening, and Grand Bargain commitments. This is the SSOT for all capacity-building planning and delivery tracking in the partnership domain.
became.after: Capacity Building Plan - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.
capacity_development
structure_contract=required,structure_pinned=true,domain=partnership,domain_verified=true

became.before: Master record for multi-partner consortia and joint programming arrangements where Ngo acts as lead agency or member. Captures consortium name, lead organization, governance structure (steering committee composition, decision-making protocols), consortium agreement reference, geographic scope, thematic focus, total funding envelope, and operational status. Supports coordination with OCHA cluster leads, IASC working groups, and pooled fund mechanisms. Essential for Grand Bargain localization commitments and joint donor reporting.
became.after: Consortium - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.
partner_registry
structure_contract=required,structure_pinned=true,domain=partnership,domain_verified=true

became.before: This association product represents the assignment of communication plans to consortia in multi-partner humanitarian coordination contexts. It captures the specific role each consortium plays in a communication plan, approval authority for consortium-branded materials, visibility requirements for donor and cluster reporting, branding guidelines for joint communications, and review status for coordinated multi-stakeholder messaging. Each record links one consortium to one communication plan with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship, supporting Grand Bargain transparency commitments and IASC coordination protocols.. Existence Justification: In humanitarian multi-partner coordination, a single consortium can be referenced in multiple communication plans (donor-specific reports, OCHA SitReps, advocacy campaigns, emergency response briefings), and a single communication plan (especially strategic plans or crisis SitReps) can cover multiple consortia or joint programming arrangements. The business actively manages consortium-specific communication requirements including approval authority, branding protocols, visibility commitments, and review workflows for each consortium-plan combination.
became.after: Consortium Communication - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.
consortium_engagement
structure_contract=required,structure_pinned=true,domain=partnership,domain_verified=true

became.before: Association record linking partner organizations to consortia, capturing each member's role (lead, co-implementer, technical advisor), contribution type, funding allocation percentage, geographic responsibility, and membership status. Tracks the full composition and role distribution within each consortium arrangement.
became.after: Consortium Member - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: Transactional record for inter-agency and cluster coordination meetings attended or hosted by Ngo. Captures meeting type (cluster, working group, bilateral, consortium), date, location, agenda items, attendees, key decisions, action items, and follow-up status. Supports accountability and institutional memory for stakeholder engagement.
became.after: Coordination Meeting - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.
consortium_engagement
structure_contract=required,structure_pinned=true,domain=partnership,domain_verified=true

became.before: Formal due diligence and partner verification master record covering legal compliance checks, sanctions screening (OFAC, EU, UN), anti-terrorism certification, financial audit review, governance verification, and regulatory standing. Includes embedded accreditation/certification tracking for CHS (Core Humanitarian Standard), Sphere compliance, HAP membership, ISO certifications, and national NGO registration status with issuing body, certificate number, issue date, expiry date, and verification status. Tracks due diligence type, completion date, outcome, risk level, next review date, and responsible staff. Required for compliance with 2 CFR 200, USAID ADS 303, and donor partner vetting regulations. This is the SSOT for all partner verification, screening, and accreditation data in the partnership domain.
became.after: Due Diligence Record - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.
agreement_governance
structure_contract=required,structure_pinned=true,domain=partnership,domain_verified=true

became.before: Transactional record for field monitoring and supportive supervision visits conducted by Ngo staff to implementing partner project sites as part of sub-award oversight obligations. Captures visit date, site location, visit purpose (programmatic monitoring, financial spot-check, safeguarding audit, asset verification), findings categorized by severity, recommendations, corrective action plans with deadlines, and follow-up verification status. Distinct from MEL domain programmatic monitoring: this product focuses on partner compliance and sub-award oversight rather than program outcome measurement. Supports donor compliance requirements for partner monitoring under USAID ADS 303 and 2 CFR 200.332.
became.after: Field Monitoring Visit - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.

Enables systematic monitoring of whether both parties are meeting their agreed commitments under each partnership instrument.
became.after: Mou Obligation - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.

Captures accreditation body, certificate number, issue date, expiry date, and verification status. Supports due diligence and quality assurance.
became.after: Partner Accreditation - core entity in the partnership domain supporting humanitarian operations.

became.before: This association product represents the Assignment between partner_org and obligation. It captures the assignment of specific compliance obligations to partner organizations, tracking partner-specific compliance status, responsible focal points, and completion tracking. Each record links one partner organization to one compliance obligation with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship: which partner must fulfill which obligation, who is responsible, when it is due, and whether it has been completed.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit operations, partner organizations are subject to multiple compliance obligations (IRS filings, donor reporting, audit requirements, registration renewals), and each compliance obligation applies to multiple partner organizations. The NGO actively manages partner compliance tracking as an operational process: assigning obligations to partners, monitoring due dates, tracking completion status, and escalating overdue items. This is not an analytical correlation but an operational business process where compliance officers create, update, and monitor partner-specific compliance assignments.

affected_objects.before: This association product represents the participation relationship between partner organizations and advocacy campaigns. It captures each partner's role, contribution type, visibility level, and approval status for their involvement in specific campaigns. Each record links one partner organization to one advocacy campaign with attributes that exist only in the context of this participation relationship. This is the operational record of partner engagement in advocacy, awareness, and fundraising campaigns managed by the communications team.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit operations, partner organizations participate in multiple advocacy campaigns simultaneously (e.g., a CSO may be involved in a humanitarian access campaign, a localization advocacy initiative, and a policy reform campaign at the same time). Each advocacy campaign involves multiple partner organizations with distinct roles (lead, supporting, implementing). The communications team actively manages these participation relationships, tracking each partner's role, contribution type, visibility level, and approval status per campaign for coordination, attribution, and reporting purposes.

affected_objects.before: This association product represents the assignment of communication plans to consortia in multi-partner humanitarian coordination contexts. It captures the specific role each consortium plays in a communication plan, approval authority for consortium-branded materials, visibility requirements for donor and cluster reporting, branding guidelines for joint communications, and review status for coordinated multi-stakeholder messaging. Each record links one consortium to one communication plan with attributes that exist only in the context of this relationship, supporting Grand Bargain transparency commitments and IASC coordination protocols.. Existence Justification: In humanitarian multi-partner coordination, a single consortium can be referenced in multiple communication plans (donor-specific reports, OCHA SitReps, advocacy campaigns, emergency response briefings), and a single communication plan (especially strategic plans or crisis SitReps) can cover multiple consortia or joint programming arrangements. became.before: This association product represents the compliance relationship between finance_fund and donor_requirement. It captures the applicability and compliance status of specific donor requirements to individual funds. Each record links one fund to one donor requirement with attributes that track when the requirement applies, compliance verification, and waiver status. Essential for grant financial management, audit preparation, and donor reporting per OMB Uniform Guidance 2 CFR 200.. Existence Justification: In NGO grant financial management, a single fund can be subject to multiple donor compliance requirements (financial reporting, audit, procurement rules, anti-terrorism certification), and a single donor requirement (e.g., quarterly financial reporting per OMB Uniform Guidance) can apply to multiple funds managed by the organization. Organizations actively manage compliance status, verification dates, and waiver requests at the fund-requirement level because compliance obligations vary by fund based on donor source, grant terms, and restriction type.

became.before: This association product represents the media relations activity between advocacy campaigns and media contacts. It captures the proactive outreach, engagement tracking, and relationship management that communications teams perform when engaging journalists and media influencers for specific campaigns. Each record links one advocacy campaign to one media contact with attributes that track the engagement lifecycle, response outcomes, and follow-up activities.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit communications operations, media relations teams actively manage which journalists and media contacts to engage for each advocacy campaign. A single campaign requires outreach to multiple media contacts (regional journalists, national outlets, specialized beat reporters), and a single media contact is engaged across multiple campaigns over time. The relationship is operationally managed with tracking of engagement dates, response outcomes, coverage types, and follow-up requirements.

became.before: Core transactional record of every outbound or inbound message exchanged with an individual constituent (donor, beneficiary, partner, volunteer, media contact). Captures channel (email, SMS, WhatsApp, post, phone, IVR), direction (inbound/outbound), subject, body excerpt, delivery status, open/click tracking, opt-out flags, consent reference, language, and linkage to the originating campaign, case, broadcast, or stewardship activity. Serves as the atomic communication event enabling full constituent interaction history and audit trail. Distinct from email_broadcast which is the batch-level record; constituent_message is the per-recipient delivery record. affected_objects.before: This association product represents the media relations activity between advocacy campaigns and media contacts. It captures the proactive outreach, engagement tracking, and relationship management that communications teams perform when engaging journalists and media influencers for specific campaigns. Each record links one advocacy campaign to one media contact with attributes that track the engagement lifecycle, response outcomes, and follow-up activities.. Existence Justification: In nonprofit communications operations, media relations teams actively manage which journalists and media contacts to engage for each advocacy campaign. A single campaign requires outreach to multiple media contacts (regional journalists, national outlets, specialized beat reporters), and a single media contact is engaged across multiple campaigns over time. The relationship is operationally managed with tracking of engagement dates, response outcomes, coverage types, and follow-up requirements.

lineage.interpretation: Define compliance domain and its products

became.before: Manages regulatory filing, statutory reporting, and organizational accountability obligations. Covers IRS 501(c)(3) filings, Charity Commission returns, IATI transparency reporting, CHS self-assessments, HAP accountability frameworks, Single Audit requirements for US federal awards, and organizational governance documentation.
became.after: Source systems: eZHACT, SAP GRC, internal audit management systems. Regulatory compliance, audit, and governance. Systems of record: TeamMate (audit), custom GRC platforms.
build_basis=vibe-modelling-agent-v0.7.1,rebuild=v2,instruction_sections_read=3

became.before: Transactional record of each finding, material weakness, significant deficiency, or questioned cost identified during a Single Audit or internal compliance audit. Captures finding reference number, finding type (material weakness, significant deficiency, questioned cost, noncompliance), federal program CFDA number, finding description, condition, criteria, cause, effect, and recommendation. Links to corrective action plans.
became.after: Transactional record of each finding, material weakness, significant deficiency, or questioned cost identified during a Single Audit or internal compliance audit. Captures finding reference number, finding type (material weakness, significant deficiency, questioned cost, noncompliance), federal program CFDA number, finding description, condition, criteria, cause, effect, and recommendation. Links to corrective action plans. became.before: Confidential master record for each alleged perpetrator named in a safeguarding investigation. Captures perpetrator code (anonymized), relationship to organization (staff, volunteer, partner staff, contractor, community member), employment or engagement status at time of incident, interim administrative measures applied (suspension, restricted duties), and final case outcome (dismissed, disciplinary action, criminal referral, cleared). Strictly access-controlled and maintained separately from workforce records to enforce investigation integrity.
became.after: Confidential master record for each alleged perpetrator named in a safeguarding investigation. Captures perpetrator code (anonymized), relationship to organization (staff, volunteer, partner staff, contractor, community member), employment or engagement status at time of incident, interim administrative measures applied (suspension, restricted duties), and final case outcome (dismissed, disciplinary action, criminal referral, cleared). Strictly access-controlled and maintained separately from workforce records to enforce investigation integrity. lineage.vibe: Add HACT (Harmonized Approach to Cash Transfers) as a first-class concept. The model currently only implies HACT via capacity_assessment and partner_compliance. Add the missing artifacts: macro_assessment, micro_assessment (with the risk rating that determines transfer modality), programme_visit, spot_check, scheduled_audit, face_form (quarterly liquidation), and a first-class IP transfer modality enum (Direct Cash Transfer / Reimbursement / Direct Payment). This is the single largest content gap for UN-agency deployments.
lineage.interpretation: Add first-class HACT framework artifacts

lineage.vibe: Add support for Cash and Voucher Assistance (CVA) to beneficiaries, distinct from cash-to-IPs covered by HACT. Add: a transfer modality enum (cash / voucher / in-kind / hybrid), a Minimum Expenditure Basket reference table, a Financial Service Provider entity (e.g. M-Pesa, RedRose, ATM card networks), and end-user verification.
lineage.interpretation: Add CVA beneficiary cash/voucher modeling

lineage.vibe: Add cold chain and vaccine-specific data for health-focused humanitarian deployments: cold_chain_equipment, batch_lot with expiry_date and who_pq_status, temperature_excursion events, vaccine_vial_monitor_state (VVM stages 1-4), and Gavi co-financing tracking.
lineage.interpretation: Add cold chain and vaccine data entities

lineage.vibe: Add the UN programme hierarchy: country_programme_document (CPD), unsdcf_outcome, strategic_plan_goal_area (e.g. Survive and Thrive, Learn, Protection, Safe and Clean Environment, Equitable Chance in Life), explicit SDG indicator alignment, and humanitarian_response_plan (anticipated by the orphan FK program.program.humanitarian_response_plan_id).
lineage.interpretation: Add UN programme hierarchy entities (CPD, UNSDCF, goal areas, HRP, SDG alignment)

lineage.vibe: Fix the accounting framework framing: finance domain comments currently reference only ASC 958 (US GAAP for nonprofits) and Form 990 (US IRS). UN agencies report under IPSAS and larger INGOs operate under multiple frameworks. Add configurable framework references in column comments, or explicit dual framing with IPSAS recognized alongside US GAAP.
lineage.interpretation: Add IPSAS / multi-framework accounting framing to finance comments

lineage.vibe: Add Databricks deployment patterns to the README so the model is a deployable Databricks lakehouse, not just a deployable SQL schema.
lineage.interpretation: Document Databricks lakehouse deployment patterns in README

lineage.vibe: Reconcile MVM/ECM placement: promote the following to MVM for humanitarian deployments — finance.exchange_rate, finance.bank_reconciliation, supply.inkind_donation, partnership.partner_risk_register, partnership.partner_compliance, field.pdm_survey, the entire safeguarding domain, and donor.soft_credit. Reconcile MVM-only stub tables with their ECM equivalents (beneficiary.needs_assessment vs beneficiary.beneficiary_needs_assessment; field.distribution_line vs field.field_distribution_line; partnership.agreement vs partnership.partnership_agreement) so that ECM is a true superset.
lineage.interpretation: Promote tables to MVM and reconcile MVM/ECM stubs so ECM is a true superset

lineage.vibe: Expand operational systems-of-record commentary in table descriptions to reflect the UN-agency stack. Comments currently anchor on Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud and Raisers Edge NXT (correct for National Committee CRMs but not UN-agency back-offices). UN agencies and large INGOs run SAP / SAP S/4HANA (VISION), eTools (programme management), InSight (BI), RAM, eZHACT, ICON (procurement), DHIS2, Kobo Toolbox, and Primero (child protection).
lineage.interpretation: Expand systems-of-record table commentary to reflect UN-agency stack

lineage.vibe: Connect the isolated program.program table: it has zero inbound and zero outbound FKs, which blocks every program-rollup query. Per P2, add column intervention_id (BIGINT) with FK to program.intervention.intervention_id.
lineage.interpretation: Connect isolated program.program via intervention_id FK

lineage.vibe: Resolve the 22 unlinked FK columns named like foreign keys but lacking foreign_key_to references (e.g. program.program.donor_id, program.program.implementing_partner_id, program.program.humanitarian_response_plan_id) by wiring them to their proper target tables.
lineage.interpretation: Wire up 22 unlinked FK columns to proper targets

lineage.vibe: Resolve the 13 cross-domain duplicate-name SSOT violations by establishing a single source of truth for each: beneficiary.beneficiary_needs_assessment vs mel.mel_needs_assessment; compliance.compliance_incident vs safeguarding.safeguarding_incident; donor.donor_fund vs finance.finance_fund; field.field_distribution_line vs supply.supply_distribution_line; field.field_team vs volunteer.volunteer_team; field.field_deployment vs volunteer.volunteer_deployment; grant.grant_amendment vs program.program_amendment; grant.grant_closeout vs program.program_closeout; grant.grant_staff_assignment vs workforce.workforce_staff_assignment; mel.mel_logframe vs program.program_logframe; partnership.partnership_agreement vs supply.supply_agreement; safeguarding.safeguarding_training_completion vs volunteer.volunteer_training_completion; safeguarding.safeguarding_policy_acknowledgment vs volunteer.volunteer_policy_acknowledgment.
lineage.interpretation: Resolve 13 cross-domain SSOT duplicate-name violations

lineage.vibe: Address the 102 self-referencing FK warnings and the 731 STRING *_code / *_number / *_key attributes that lack FKs to lookup tables by linking them to proper lookup/reference tables where appropriate.
lineage.interpretation: Fix self-referencing FK warnings and link *_code/*_number/*_key STRING attrs to lookup tables

lineage.vibe: Add PII classification tags. The agent flagged 444 attributes matching person-data patterns without pii_ classification tags. Apply classification tags (pii_beneficiary_protected, pii_donor, pii_staff, pii_de_identified) mapped to Unity Catalog tag values, and document a masking-policy set in the README, since humanitarian beneficiary data (protection status, displacement, vulnerability, biometrics, case notes) carries higher-than-commercial sensitivity and customers cannot apply dynamic masking, RLS, or pass a donor audit without it.
lineage.interpretation: Apply pii_ classification tags to 444 person-data attributes and document masking policy

lineage.vibe: Enrich the skeleton/stub product volunteer.volunteer_deployment2, which currently has only PK/FK columns and zero (or fewer than 5) data attributes; derive a full set of real business data attributes that make it a usable entity from its business context.
lineage.interpretation: Enrich stub volunteer.volunteer_deployment2 with full data attributes

lineage.vibe: Review and expand the 6 thin products that have only 4-8 data attributes where Section 2 or domain norms warrant more depth: beneficiary.community_intervention (6), grant.award_site_allocation (7), donor.segment_membership (8), field.assessment_participation (8), volunteer.tool_authorization (8), partnership.campaign_participation (8).
lineage.interpretation: Expand 6 thin products with additional data attributes

lineage.vibe: P1: Rename product volunteer.volunteer_deployment2 to volunteer_redeployment, because 'volunteer_deployment2' is a stub/duplicate name suggesting an accidental duplicate.
lineage.interpretation: Rename volunteer.volunteer_deployment2 to volunteer_redeployment

lineage.vibe: P3: Connect finance.budget_version by adding column budget_id (BIGINT) with FK to finance.budget.budget_id, because budget_version currently has only a self-ref and one inbound reference.
lineage.interpretation: Connect finance.budget_version via budget_id FK

lineage.interpretation: Connect technology.backup_schedule via user_account_id FK

lineage.vibe: P7: Connect workforce.competency_framework by adding column org_unit_id (BIGINT) with FK to workforce.org_unit.org_unit_id, because competency_framework only has a self-ref.
lineage.interpretation: Connect workforce.competency_framework via org_unit_id FK

after.sql: SELECT 1 AS readme_placeholder
after.description: Databricks Lakehouse Deployment: This model is deployable as a Databricks Unity Catalog lakehouse. Use Delta Lake tables partitioned by domain schema. Apply Unity Catalog tags for PII classification: pii_beneficiary_protected (protection status, displacement, vulnerability, biometrics, case notes), pii_donor (donor PII), pii_staff (employee/volunteer PII), pii_de_identified (aggregated/anonymized). Dynamic masking policies: MASK(pii_beneficiary_protected) -> SHA2 in non-prod; MASK(pii_donor) -> REDACT in non-prod; MASK(pii_staff) -> REDACT in non-prod; pii_de_identified -> no masking required. Row-Level Security (RLS): apply by country_office_id and intervention_id for multi-tenant isolation. Operational systems of record (UN-agency stack): Systems of record: SAP S/4HANA (VISION), eTools, InSight, RAM, eZHACT, ICON (procurement), DHIS2, Kobo Toolbox, Primero (child protection), Salesforce Nonprofit Cloud, Raisers Edge NXT.

after.sql: SELECT 1 AS masking_policy_placeholder
after.description: PII Masking Policy Set for Unity Catalog: Tag pii_beneficiary_protected: applies to beneficiary protection status, displacement history, vulnerability scores, biometric data, case notes. Policy: SHA2 hash in dev/test, full access in prod with RLS. Tag pii_donor: applies to donor names, contact info, gift amounts, wealth screening. Policy: REDACT in dev/test, full access in prod for authorized fundraising roles. Tag pii_staff: applies to staff names, payroll, disciplinary records, performance reviews. Policy: REDACT in dev/test, full access in prod for HR roles. Tag pii_de_identified: applies to aggregated/anonymized data. Policy: no masking required. Humanitarian beneficiary data carries higher-than-commercial sensitivity per IASC guidelines. Dynamic masking via Unity Catalog column masks; RLS via row filters on country_office_id.
